index_title: Sparse graphs, original parity/Hasse and exact gate separation
scope: Preparation for OTHER Lean projects. Seven source results: the full labelled sparse-graph proof, original SAP-free finite Hasse indices, independent relative exact separation and maximal exact gates. No Lean code.
scope_explanation: statement and proof. Hasse has no exact-Helly import; closure separation and maximal gates are independent consumers of RAW exact calculus.

assumptions.name: Actual original source
assumptions.statement: One inhabited transitive homogeneous complete finite symmetric binary source, with actual represented orbitals and semantic homomorphic CCO. No SAP, primitivity, NR2 or countability is used. Subclaims state when only elementary orbital algebra suffices.

assumptions.name: Finite combinatorial foundation
assumptions.statement: Ordinary classical finite graph/probability reasoning, real exp/log inequalities and Archimedean integer choice. The lower-tail bound and sparse graph theorem are proved here, not imported as Erdős or Chernoff axioms.

imports.name: RAW exact product and support Helly
imports.statement: Nonempty original equality-inclusive exact relations are product-closed and 2-Helly. In particular three pairwise-intersecting exact supports intersect. Heterogeneous ball Helly is not needed by this module.

definitions.name: Finite independent edge labels
definitions.statement: For positive q,r,g and n>c=128rq log(q+1), independent unordered pairs carry 0 with probability 1-c/n and each positive label with probability c/(nr).

definitions.name: Robust colouring-label counts
definitions.statement: X(kappa,h) counts monochromatic pairs with the label h of their common vertex colour; mu is its expectation.

definitions.name: Original symmetric orbital source
definitions.statement: One inhabited original transitive homogeneous finite complete symmetric binary source; finitely many actual pair orbitals including logical Id. The only direct semantic CCO application in this module is orbital bipartiteness; the separately imported RAW exact calculus has its own CCO proof. No SAP or countability is used.

definitions.name: Full invariant lattice and relative index
definitions.statement: All actual invariant equivalences, ordered by inclusion. [F:E] counts E-classes in any F-class, uniformly by transitivity. Endpoints need not be exact.

definitions.name: RAW walk parity
definitions.statement: Y_c, O_c are the even- and odd-walk relations of an old diversity atom; X_c is connectivity. Length zero is allowed in Y, with a later positive even-word representation.

definitions.name: Original full exact relation
definitions.statement: A nonempty relation expressible as a finite intersection of actual atomic word profiles; empty restrictions give Top, empty word Id. Nonempty refers to the evaluated result. ExEq is only the exact part of the full lattice.

definitions.name: K-relative powers and closure
definitions.statement: For exact equivalence K and symmetric exact K-bisaturated A containing K, A^[0]=K and A^[n]=A^n for n>0; stable power is <A>.

definitions.name: Two-sheet source data
definitions.statement: Invariant Y<X of relative index two; Y and O=X\Y exact, but X need not be exact.

definitions.name: Maximal exact gate candidate
definitions.statement: Inclusion-maximal exact equivalence K with Y<=K and K meet X=Y; F=K join X and t=K;O;K.

definitions.name: Actual quotient and bridge
definitions.statement: Let K be an actual full exact invariant equivalence. Use the original action on M/K with all actual quotient orbitals. A bridge R at K is nonempty, invariant and full exact and satisfies K;R=R and R;R^converse=K; quotient-object identity is K.

source.anchor: Given a full exact invariant equivalence

claims.name: Colouring counts and mean
claims.statement: Same-colour pair count N>=(n²/q-n)/2>=n²/(4q) for n>=2q; requested labels give independent Bernoulli variables of parameter c/(nr), hence mu>=cn/(4rq).

claims.name: Elementary exponential lower tail
claims.statement: E(exp(-X))<=(1-p/2)^N<=exp(-mu/2); Markov yields Pr(X<mu/4)<=exp(-mu/4). No Chernoff import.

claims.name: Finite union and short cycles
claims.statement: Choose n by the four explicit N02 bounds. Simultaneous robust counts and at most 4B short cycles have positive probability; no independence between these two events is needed.

claims.name: Deletion and labelled sparsity
claims.statement: Delete at most 4B edges, one per remaining original short cycle. Every robust count stays positive, implying the full q-colour/r-label property.

claims.name: High chromatic girth and connected extraction
claims.statement: The r=1 case has no proper q-colouring; some connected component retains that property and girth>g. Do not claim component extraction preserves the r>1 labelled property.

claims.name: Original elementary RAW algebra
claims.statement: Atoms are actual pair orbitals; NONEMPTY invariant relations are serial/coserial. Invariant relations compose associatively and commute by symmetry of ALL orbitals. The full invariant-equivalence lattice is finite; joins are represented products. No exact Helly is used.

claims.name: Transposition with class bijection
claims.statement: For F=E join X and K=E meet X, [K,X] and [E,F] are order-isomorphic. Separately X[a]/K -> F[a]/E is a bijection, so [X:K]=[F:E].

claims.name: Index-two covers and finite chain indices
claims.statement: Relative index two gives a full-lattice cover. Transitivity gives uniform indices; finite containing indices make intermediate factors finite, and chain indices multiply.

claims.name: Cycle homomorphism templates
claims.statement: Even cycles fold onto one edge. An odd cycle of length k>ell maps onto an old odd ell-cycle by adding (k-ell)/2 backtracks. These are homomorphisms, not embeddings.

claims.name: Finite-relative orbital bipartiteness
claims.statement: For E<F of finite relative index n and old atom c<=F\E, an odd cycle would give a connected high-chromatic graph all of whose cycles map to c. CCO then yields a forbidden proper n-colouring inside one F-class.

claims.name: Positive even and odd profile stabilization
claims.statement: Seriality gives Id<=c²; parity chains stabilize in the finite support lattice. A common positive even threshold represents all even and odd walks by single positive RAW words.

claims.name: Index-two connectivity seed
claims.statement: Y and O are nonempty exact profiles; Y<X=Y union O<=F has [X:Y]=2 and X not<=E. X need not be exact, Y need not contain E.

claims.name: Full finite-index Hasse cover induction
claims.statement: Induct on height of F. Transpose the index-two seed to K=E meet X; if K differs from Y, transpose distinct coatoms again to a cover with strictly smaller upper endpoint Y and the same finite index.

claims.name: All finite relative indices are powers of two
claims.statement: Multiply finite cover indices along a saturated interval chain. Equality E=F gives 1=2^0. No endpoint exactness is assumed.

claims.name: Stable K-relative exact closures
claims.statement: Relative powers start at K, increase, remain exact and K-bisaturated, and stabilize to invariant exact equivalences.

claims.name: Least positive exponents and atom
claims.statement: A hypothetical common closure atom outside K gives least n>=1 for B and then least m>=1 for A.

claims.name: Minimality exclusion
claims.statement: The selected c is not in A^[m-1];B^[n-1]. Atomic Peirce plus closure equivalence handles b outside K; K-saturation handles b in K, including m=1,n=1.

claims.name: Outer-saturated three-domain obstruction
claims.statement: T=A^[m-1];c;B^[n-1] is nonempty exact and K-bisaturated by its outer factors. It meets A and B but avoids K; a K-intersection would force Id<=T and violate C17.

claims.name: Relative closure separation
claims.statement: The exact supports A,B,T violate three-domain RAW Helly unless <A> meet <B>=K. No ball Helly, Hasse or CRT is needed.

claims.name: Identity separation
claims.statement: Specialize relative closure separation to K=Id; real equality is an exact word profile.

claims.name: Two-sheet complement geometry
claims.statement: For invariant Y<X of index two, O;O=Y. Transposing K meet X=Y gives [K join X:K]=2.

claims.name: Finite maximal exact candidate
claims.statement: The candidate set is finite and nonempty (contains Y), so an inclusion-maximal K exists.

claims.name: Exact gate and quotient involution
claims.statement: t=K;O;K is nonempty exact, K-bisaturated, F=K disjoint-union t, t;t=K. Only t/K is a fixed-point-free involution graph; t on real points need not be functional.

claims.name: Original exact dominance
claims.statement: Every original exact equivalence Z>K contains t: Z meet X is Y or X; the former violates maximality, the latter gives O<=Z.

claims.name: Actual quotient exact pullback
claims.statement: Each actual quotient orbital pulls back to K;a;K, equality to K. Surjectivity and saturation give product pullback; words and finite intersections therefore preserve exactness under inverse image.

claims.name: Quotient dominance and nonidentity bridge
claims.statement: Pull back any nontrivial quotient exact equivalence, apply C24 and project. The gate equations already make t a nonidentity exact isotropy bridge; rigid character is a consumer, not an input.

tasks.name: Robust labelled sparse graphs
tasks.acceptance: Prove the finite probability construction, explicit sufficient n bounds, bounded deletion and the connected one-label graph provider.

tasks.name: Original equivalence/index geometry
tasks.acceptance: Prove original commutation, full-lattice transposition, the actual quotient-class bijection and finite relative index multiplication.

tasks.name: Orbital parity and full Hasse
tasks.acceptance: Prove bipartiteness using homomorphic CCO, positive parity profiles and cover-height induction in the full invariant lattice.

tasks.name: Relative exact separation
tasks.acceptance: Use RAW exact products/three-set Helly; retain K as zeroth power and outer-factor saturation.

tasks.name: Original maximal exact gate
tasks.acceptance: Prove gate equations and dominance for all original exact Z>K, without exactness of X or separation/Hasse imports.

tasks.name: Quotient/bridge consumer
tasks.acceptance: Prove actual quotient word pullback and dominant quotient involution; no general exact descent or rigid-character input.

controls.check: F2^3 full invariant subspace lattice: all finite relative indices, covers, class-bijection transpositions and a nondistributive M3 interval.
Triangle-free four-chromatic Mycielski C5 graph defeats finite K3 while every cycle maps to K3; missing CCO must not pass unnoticed.
Actual F2² translation supports show closure separation fails without exactness of the two supports A,B.
Two three-point sheets: nontrivial exact K, t²=K, three real successors per point, but a two-point quotient involution. This is an algebra control, not a CCO assertion.
Explicit sparse-graph n inequalities at q=r=1 and further small parameter values; even folds and odd-cycle backtrack lengths.
